title: Knowledge service (OKS)
description: Turns the knowledge service and data file declared by the session's workspace into seventeen native tools (search / references / info / check_intent / query / create_data / jq_transform / jq_transform_into / chart / view / report / artifacts / collect / work_read / work_write / work_edit / work_delete): find a key by name or description, walk the reference graph backwards from a key, read a node by key, validate a business question into named intents (the ones that pass come back with a key that the query must carry verbatim, and the tool re-hashes it before running), then answer it with real rows over a read-only connection. Each success is saved to a result file under the workspace's .oks/data/, so the rows stay out of the model context: explore them with jq_transform (named inputs, each of which may be any product — an envelope, a figure, a table or a report, read in place with no intermediate file; each entry carries its own root — a jq dot path, .data by default, .origin for the source chain, .meta or the whole {meta, origin, data}; without a program the result is the {name: slice} object itself and pick takes one part of it back, while a program goes into a .work/*.jq file named by the byFile argument, so jq syntax never sits next to the JSON of the call itself; that directory is read, created, edited and pruned only by work_read / work_write / work_edit / work_delete, whose scope is enforced to .work/) and materialise a result for the next step with jq_transform_into, which writes a new envelope whose origin carries the whole source chain; data the agent supplies itself goes through create_data first, so it becomes the same kind of envelope and can be referenced the same way. No model is baked in — a workspace opts in with an oks.json, and the agent explores the domain starting from the opaque key "index". Figures are drawn on the server into SVG files in the workspace: oks_chart takes its rows from a saved envelope only (src — queried rows, a computed result, or rows created with create_data), embeds the rows it drew, its specification and the whole source chain in the SVG, and returns a markdown line that the agent puts into its reply to show the figure there. oks_view turns saved data into a markdown display piece (.oks/figures/ — a table you can open and read, with its source chain and final data hidden in a leading HTML comment), which renders both in the reply and in a report. oks_report assembles several figures, tables and prose into one self-contained HTML report — figures inlined as SVG, tables as real <table> elements, with a table of contents and captions, and a report-level provenance structure holding each display item's final data and whole source chain (it fails outright when a referenced material is missing or the provenance grows past its cap); a report's display items and any product's source chain are read with the same jq_transform, because root can hand over .origin instead of .data — reading data and reading provenance are one path, with no dedicated tool and no cross-check of the recorded data file. An HTML report is handed over with the present tool and read in the sidebar, not in the reply body. Three helpers ride along: time_now / time_calc for standard time representations and calendar arithmetic, and va_ask, which consults a vocabulary helper the plugin owns (a top-level agent on the same preset and workspace, sharing the process-wide index, archived while idle): it prepares that helper itself by putting role, the whole vocabulary and the working method into its system prompt — assembly sends no message at all — and, after every answer, collapses the question-and-answer into one fixed-text marker — so between questions the helper sees only vocabulary, method and the current question, while the session log stays append-only. Reports are temporary by default — an unpinned one is removed about an hour after it was produced, and the internal materials (data and figures) are reclaimed on their own window; both are configurable per workspace in oks.json under retention (auto runs on the write path, manual is what the explicit collect tool and the sidebar clean-up button use); the user decides what to keep with a pin in the sidebar, and oks_artifacts lists what exists. Reports live in artifacts/, internal materials and state in .oks/.
